Name: Mr. Piyush Shaha
Bio: Mr. Piyush Shaha is an accomplished academician with extensive experience in the fields of Statistics, Operations Management, and Business Administration. He holds multiple postgraduate degrees, including an M.Sc. in Statistics, M.B.A. in Operations, and M.Com. in Business Administration, along with a B.Sc. in Statistics. He has also qualified the SET (State Eligibility Test) in Mathematical Sciences and is currently pursuing a Ph.D. in Statistics. Prior to this, he held key academic positions at several reputed institutions, including NMIMS University, St. John College of Humanities and Science, The New College – Kolhapur, and others. His teaching career spans over 15 years, covering diverse roles such as full-time faculty, visiting professor, academic coordinator, and secondary school mathematics teacher. He began his academic journey as a Visiting Professor (CHB) in 2005, and since then, has consistently contributed to higher education through teaching, academic administration, and assessment roles. Mr. Shaha has served as an invigilator, moderator, and paper setter across various reputed institutions affiliated to Shivaji University, Mumbai University, Bharati Vidyapeeth, Tilak Maharashtra Vidyapeeth, Mahatma Phule Krishi Vidyapeeth, and YCMOU. With a strong academic foundation and versatile teaching portfolio, Mr. Piyush Shaha is deeply committed to student success, academic excellence, and continuous learning in the domain of statistics and business education.

Bio: Mandar S Sapre holds a Ph.D. in the Application of Optimization Techniques in Mesh Smoothing from the Faculty of Mechanical Engineering at Symbiosis International (Deemed University). He received his Master of Technology in CAD/CAM from Symbiosis Institute of Technology and his Bachelor of Engineering in Production Engineering from Mumbai University. Currently, he is working as a Research Assistant Professor at the Institute of Artificial Intelligence, MIT World Peace University, starting in December 2024. His research interests include Engineering Mathematics, Finite Element Analysis, Numerical Methods, Optimization Techniques, Machine Learning, Cohort Intelligence, Hybrid Metaheuristics, Operation Research, Application Development, and Programming. He has 22 publications in peer-reviewed journals, conferences, and chapters. He has so far guided 10 masters and over 90 UG students. He is a regular reviewer of different Elsevier journals. Mandar has also served as session chair for a few international conferences. Apart from academics, Mandar enjoys reading novels and listening to and singing Indian music. He loves to travel and experience different cultures.

Bio: Chandrashekhar D Bobade is an Assistant Professor and Research coordinator at the School of Health Science and Technology. He has a total of 10 years of teaching experience and 6 years of research experience. Chandrashekhar secured distinction from his first to final year of B.Pharm and was awarded Sir Ratan Tata's meritorious scholarship from the second year of graduation to the end of post-graduation. He completed his post-graduation education in Pharmaceutics from Shivaji University, Kolhapur in 2008 with the First class and received the best outgoing student of the year award during his masters. Chandrashekhar has received research grants of 1.20 L from BCUD, Savitribai Phule Pune University, and has experience writing DBT, SERB POWER grants. He has published high impact research in journals like Nanoscale and Nanoscale Advances with impact factor 5 and 7.5, respectively, and has 3 patent applications and 14 oral research and development presentations in international conferences at AIIMS, IIT New Delhi. His research area mainly includes surface modifications of Biomaterials, Chronotherapeutics, and polymeric drug delivery systems. Chandrashekhar's team has published nanomaterials that support the growth of 3D cells more effectively than traditional 2D cell culture techniques by simulating the ex vivo tissue milieu using multiple components on a glass substrate. Advanced materials with various physico-chemical properties, such as multiwall carbon nanotubes (CNT), graphene (G), bovine serum albumin (BSA), and iron oxide magnetic nanoparticles, were chemically combined to create 3D nanosubstrates. Chandrashekhar is a passionate advocate of Problem and Project-based learning in his classroom teaching. He is also a columnist for advanced career guidance in pharmacy, National Education Policy 2020, and innovative pedagogy in leading newspapers like Maharashtra Times, Loksatta, etc. Chandrashekhar has delivered invited talks on innovative pedagogy and is actively involved in professional activities for the students' development. He is a lifetime member of the Indian Pharmaceutical Association and Association of Pharmaceutical Teachers in India. Chandrashekhar is voluntarily affiliated with the Indian Pharmaceutical Association Pune branch as Vice President.

Bio: Dr. Mukul S. Godbole currently serves as an Assistant Professor in the Dept. of Biosciences and Technology, MIT-WPU. Dr. Godbole is a cancer cell biologist. His doctoral work focused on elucidating the mechanism of action of progesterone in human breast cancer. The work performed at ACTREC–TMC identified an intricate genomic network that suppresses breast cancer cell migration and invasion in response to progesterone, independent of progesterone receptor expression. Dr. Godbole has published 11 research articles and reviews in peer-reviewed journals of international repute. Dr. Godbole’s research interests include breast cancer, steroid hormones and receptors, cancer cell biology, metastasis, and microbiomes. Dr. Godbole serves as a Guest Editor for the ‘Cancer and Microbiome’ and ‘Cancer Metastasis: Mechanisms and Treatment’ special issues of Cancer Reports. He is also the Editorial Board Member of Cancer Reports. Further, Dr. Godbole serves as an Early Career Reviewer for the Journal of Biological Chemistry. He also serves as a peer-reviewer for Cancer Reports, Clinical Breast Cancer, BBA–Reviews on Cancer, Experimental Cell Research, Heliyon, npj Biofilms and Microbiomes, Microbial Cell, Cellular Signalling, PLoS One, Frontiers in Cellular and Infection Microbiology, Gut Microbes Reports, and STAR Protocols. Moreover, he has previously worked as a Freelance Science Editor with Cactus Communications Pvt. Ltd. for three years and edited 410 manuscripts. Name: Dr. Nithya N Kutty
Bio: Dr. Nithya N. Kutty has completed her doctoral study from IIT Kharagpur. Her doctoral study was focused on dynamics of scent volatiles synthesis, storage and emission in flowers of tuberose, a widely cultivated ornamental plant in Asian countries. During her doctoral study (through CSIR JRF/SRF fellowship), she has also carried out collaborative research work in the area of metabolite profiling from plant endophytes, hairy roots of carrots and studied the effect of gamma rays on floral volatiles. She has also presented her research work in several national and international conferences. She pursued her post-graduation (M Tech) in Agricultural biotechnology from IIT Kharagpur and completed her graduation (B Tech Biotechnology) from JNTU Hyderabad. Her research area of interests includes plant specialized metabolism, plant-microbe interactions, plant volatiles and metabolomics. Presently she is teaching basic and applied courses at undergraduate, postgraduate and doctoral levels. She is a recognized PhD supervisor of the university. She also mentors students for their research project. Recently, she could secure "DST Young scientist and Technologist" grant under which she is working on vaporization of waste marigold flowers using natural deep eutectic solvents. Dr. Kutty could also complete EMBO lab leadership course with full support from EMBO. She also holds two published Indian patents and one granted patent through her research in the domain of green chemistry. Name: Dr. Soma Mishra
Bio: Dr. Soma Mishra is an Environmentalist and active in research, writing, and teaching for over 12 years. She holds a Ph.D. in Environmental Engineering from the Indian Institute of Technology, Roorkee, an M.Tech. in Environmental Engineering from NIFFT, Ranchi. She also earned her M.Sc.in Environmental Sciences from Sambalpur University and B.Sc. in Environment and Water Management from Ranchi University. She received a DAAD fellowship and worked in the University of applied sciences, Dresden as a Visiting Scientist. She is actively associated with the River Bank Filtration group in India and abroad. She worked on many projects related to Lake/Riverbank filtration which are funded by European Commission. Earlier, she worked as a Climate Scientist and Associate Director with Sustain Labs Paris. She also worked as an Assistant Professor in prestigious institutions like Maharaja Sayajirao University of Baroda and Marwadi University. Her research’s overarching objective is to ascertain, broaden and develop various dimensions of emerging contaminants in the water systems and their effective removal. She has experience in the degradation and detoxification of complex industrial and municipal wastewater pollutants by bioaugmentation and phytoremediation approaches for sustainable development. She also specializes in the field of use of wastewater for agricultural purposes and the management of solid waste at the organizational level by sustainable approaches. She also gained experience in understanding indoor air pollution and its remedies and other associated problems relevant to climate change. Apart from academics and research, she is passionate about social services and worked for many rural communities to solve the issues related to polluted drinking water. She is a founder of SustainOEarth, through which she works for small scale industries and societies to resolve issues related to water and waste management. She is also associated with organizations that worked in the field of women’s Entrepreneurship development for rural artisans.

Name: Dr. Nilesh Bajad
Bio: Dr. Nilesh Bajad completed his Doctoral degree from the Indian Institute of Technology (BHU), Varanasi, under the Prime Minister’s Research Fellowship (PMRF), India’s most prestigious doctoral fellowship program. He also earned his Master’s degree from IIT (BHU), where he developed a strong foundation in Pharmaceutical Chemistry. His Ph.D. research, titled “Exploring the diagnostic and therapeutic potential of rationally designed and synthesized novel multifunctional ligands for Alzheimer’s disease,” focused on the design, synthesis, and biological evaluation of multifunctional small molecules integrating both therapeutic and diagnostic (theranostic) functionalities for Alzheimer’s disease (AD). The work aimed to develop novel agents capable of crossing the blood–brain barrier, detecting amyloid aggregates, and modulating key enzymatic and oxidative pathways implicated in AD pathogenesis. Dr. Bajad possesses experience in organic synthesis, biophysical and biochemical assays, cell-based evaluations, assay development, and animal model studies. His research lies at the interface of medicinal chemistry, drug discovery, and neuroscience, driven by a strong motivation to translate chemical innovations into promising biological and therapeutic outcomes. His research findings have been published in leading journals such as ACS Chemical Neuroscience, Talanta, Bioorganic Chemistry, International Journal of Biological Macromolecules, and European Journal of Medicinal Chemistry, reflecting his significant contributions to neurotherapeutics and medicinal chemistry. His long-term vision focuses on neuroscience-driven drug discovery, integrating chemistry and biology to design innovative theranostic and therapeutic agents for neurodegenerative diseases. Bio: Anand J Kulkarni holds a PhD in Artificial Intelligence (AI) based Distributed Optimization from Nanyang Technological University, Singapore, MS in AI from University of Regina, Canada. He worked as Postdoctoral Research Fellow at Odette School of Business, University of Windsor, Canada. Anand is a Bachelor of Engineering in Mechanical Engineering from the Shivaji University, India and holds a Diploma from Board of Technical Education, Mumbai, India. Since 2021, he is working as Research Professor and Associate Director of the Institute of Artificial Intelligence at the MIT-WPU, Pune, India. His research interests include AI based Nature Inspired optimization algorithms, and self-organizing systems. Anand pioneered optimization methodologies such as Cohort Intelligence, Ideology Algorithm, Expectation Algorithm, Socio Evolution & Learning Optimization Algorithm, Leader-Advocate-Believer Algorithm and Snail Homing and Mating Search Algorithm. Anand has published over 90 research papers in peer-reviewed reputed journals, chapters and conferences along with 7 authored and 15 edited books. Name: Dr. Ganesh Suresh Jadhav
Bio: Dr. Ganesh Jadhav is the Associate Professor & Program Director, School of Design at Dr. Vishwanath Karad MIT World Peace University (MIT-WPU), Pune, and a design academician with a rare blend of deep research, industry practice, and academic leadership. He holds a PhD in Design from IIT Guwahati, with specialized expertise in Ergonomics, Product Design, and Industrial Design, and over 16 years of combined academic and industrial experience. Dr. Jadhav has worked with leading organizations such as Philips India Pvt. Ltd., bringing strong industry relevance into design education through practice-driven pedagogy and innovation-led mentoring. At MIT-WPU, he has played a pivotal role in curriculum development, program leadership, PhD program establishment, accreditation processes (NAAC/NIRF), and industry-academia integration. As an educator, researcher, and mentor, Dr. Jadhav is committed to shaping future- ready designers who combine creativity, empathy, technology, and societal relevance. Dr. Ganesh S. Jadhav brings over 16 years of combined academic and industrial experience in the fields of Product Design, Industrial Design, and Occupational Ergonomics. He holds a Ph.D. with a focus on Product/Industrial Design and Occupational Ergonomics, and his academic journey is marked by a deep commitment to interdisciplinary and industry-relevant research and education. Dr. Jadhav has worked for five years with Vishay (Philips) Components India Pvt. Ltd., Pune, where he was responsible for overseeing comprehensive maintenance activities. His industrial experience includes the deft application of preventive, predictive, planned, and corrective maintenance strategies across various machinery and systems. As a passionate educator and researcher, Dr. Jadhav has published extensively in reputed national and international journals and conferences. He actively collaborates with professionals and students across diverse creative disciplines and integrates design thinking with engineering applications in both academic and industrial contexts. He has filed 20 Indian patents and 1 South African patent, reflecting his commitment to innovation and practical problem-solving. His work often bridges the gap between ergonomic design principles and real-world production environments, aiming to enhance both productivity and user well-being. Dr. Jadhav is also a Life Member of ISTE (Indian Society for Technical Education).

Bio: Associate Prof. Dr. Vijayapandi Pandy is an experienced academician and researcher working in the School of Pharmacy at MIT World Peace University in Pune, Maharashtra, India. He completed his B.Pharm with first-class honors in 1997 and M.Pharm (Pharmacology) with the first rank from SCS College of Pharmacy, Harapanahalli, Karnataka, India, in 2000. Dr. Pandy obtained his Ph.D. in psychopharmacology from the prestigious Birla Institute of Technology and Science, Pilani (BITS-Pilani), India. Dr. Pandy's primary research interests are in the psychopharmacological evaluation of psychoactive natural products for novel drug discovery in the treatment of nicotine dependence and withdrawal using animal models. He is a life member of several professional bodies, including the Tamil Nadu Pharmacy Council, Indian Pharmacological Society, Laboratory Animal Scientist's Association (LASA, INDIA), Association of Pharmaceutical Teachers of India (APTI), and Indian Pharmacy Graduate Association. Dr. Pandy has over 20 years of experience in teaching and research, having worked in India, Malaysia, Libya, and Ethiopia. He has published over 65 research and review articles in peer-reviewed journals and is a reviewer for various national and international journals. He has also received research grants such as BKP, UMRG, and HIR-MOHE, Malaysia, and recently completed a research project (CRG/2023/005830/BHS; Sanctioned amount Rs 34 lakhs) as PI from DST-SERB, India in November 2022. He was awarded the Mahatma Gandhi Samman Award from the NRI Welfare Society in Bangkok, Thailand, on 27 May 2017. Dr. Pandy has successfully supervised six Ph.D. and twelve M.Pharm research projects and is currently supervising one Ph.D. and two M.Pharm projects. His expertise and contributions to the field make him a valuable member of the academic and research community."

Bio: Himangi Neve is an Assistant Professor in the Bioengineering Department of Dr. Vishwanath Karad MIT World Peace University in Pune, India. She has a master’s degree in polymer engineering and is now pursuing a PhD in chemical engineering. She has 11 years of combined job experience in industry and academia. Her research focuses on developing more effective and efficient bioconversion technologies for converting agricultural waste into high-value items, as well as evaluating the significance of life cycle assessment in processes ranging from waste collection to product distribution. She has produced over 5 research articles in international journals and 3 book chapters, and has garnered numerous accolades, including two Best Paper awards at international conferences and a runner-up team at the MITWPU Hackathon. She also won a Rs. 3 lakh research grant from MITWPU, as well as Rs. 1 lakh in the Hackathon. Himangi has also completed a number of waste management consulting projects for national and multinational companies. She has also published an Indian patent. In addition to her teaching and research responsibilities, Himangi is the department’s IQAC, Exam, Infrastructure, and Rural Immersion Coordinator.

Name: Prof. Hossein Martin Fazeli
Bio: Hossein Martin Fazeli is a distinguished Iranian writer, producer, and director who has been an A-list filmmaker in North America for many years and currently serves as a Professor of Practice at Dadasaheb Phalke International Film School. With over two decades of experience in producing, directing, and writing fiction and non-fiction television and films, Fazeli has built an illustrious career marked by his extensive international collaborations across more than a dozen countries. His works have been broadcast globally on leading networks such as CBC, BBC, ARTE, and Canal+, earning 37 international awards and critical acclaim. Fazeli’s films often explore themes of human rights, women’s rights, and minority rights, underscoring his commitment to social justice. He has collaborated with prominent organizations, including the United Nations Development Programme (UNDP), the European Commission, and Nonviolence International, contributing to impactful film and television projects and national and regional campaigns. One of his landmark productions, the 2007 documentary “The Tale of Two Nazanins”, spotlighted the plight of a teenage girl imprisoned on death row in Iran. Broadcast on major international networks such as BBC and CNN, the film ignited a global campaign that ultimately saved her life, exemplifying Fazeli’s ability to harness the power of storytelling for change. In 2008, Fazeli was honored by the Sundance Institute, participating in their International Filmmakers Award program. As a sought-after speaker, he has lectured globally on the evolving landscape of film production and conducted workshops at prestigious institutions like Simon Fraser University (Canada), SOAS University of London (UK), Aarhus University (Denmark), and the European Film Academy. In addition to his filmmaking, Fazeli is a celebrated Persian poet, known under the pen name “Naanaam”. Currently, Fazeli is completing three human rights-related films, including “PHOOLAN”, a docu-drama on the life and legacy of India’s Bandit Queen.

Bio: Neurodegenerative disorders, characterized by the accumulation of protein aggregates in the human brain, represent a significant threat to human well-being for which no therapeutic treatment is available. Dr. Mandar's research attempts to address this condition by exploring the effect of herbal extracts on protein aggregation. During his doctoral research, he discovered an Ayurvedic extract known as Triphala to be capable of inhibiting the formation of protein aggregates in vitro. Further, the very challenging task of identification of the active ingredient of Triphala was successfully achieved and the mechanistic insights into the inhibition process were obtained. After his PhD, he worked as an industrial R&D scientist on the development of generic equivalent of the following: (a) Peptide hormones involved in controlling blood glucose levels (b) Peptides to treat short bowel syndrome (c) Vitamin supplements. During his short tenure at IISER Berhampur, he was in the pursuit of unravelling the structure and dynamics of complex protein enzymes by NMR spectroscopy. Going ahead, he is interested in targeting three interesting research directions: (i) Investigating the effect of Triphala and its active ingredient on protein aggregate-induced cell death by ex vivo cell toxicity assays. (ii) Developing drug delivery systems for the anti-aggregation compounds to cross the blood-brain barrier. (iii) Studying the phase separation and aggregation behaviour of peptide hormones involved in controlling blood glucose levels. Subjects Taught Chemical Biology

Bio: Dr. Bharat S. Chaudhari has pursued the BE in Industrial Electronics from Amravati University in 1989 and then METelE and PhD in Engineering from Jadavpur University, Kolkata, India, in 1993 and 2000, respectively. After being a Full Professor in Electronics and Telecommunication Engineering with the Pune Institute of Computer Technology and the Dean and Principal of the International Institute of Information Technology, Pune, he joined MIT World Peace University (then MIT Pune) in 2014 as a Professor. Currently, he is working as a Senior Professor (Higher Administrative Group) in Electronics and Communication Engineering and Dean – Research and Development. He held additional responsibilities as Dean of Academics (July 2021 - Sept 2022), Associate Dean - Faculty of Engineering and Technology (Feb 2020 - June 2023), and Head of the School of Electrical/Electronics and Telecommunication Engineering (July 2017 - December 2023) at MIT World Peace University. With 35 years of experience in teaching and research, he has authored more than 125 research papers in wireless, telecom, and optical networks and edited several conference proceedings and four books. He has four granted patents, and two patents are in the published stage. Since 2007, Dr. Chaudhari has been appointed as a Visiting Scientist (Simons Associate/Regular Associate) to ICTP, a Tier I research organization of UNESCO established by Nobel Laureate Dr. Abdus Salam in Trieste, Italy. Dr. Chaudhari has successfully executed several research and consultancy projects and accomplished international research collaborations. He has delivered technical talks at various conferences and platforms in different countries. Dr. Chaudhari is a recipient of the 2020 IETE N V Gadadhar Memorial Award for outstanding contribution in fostering research and education, the MAEER Pune’s Ideal Teacher Award 2015, and the Young Scientist Research Grant from the Department of Science and Technology, Government of India, in 2003. Dr. Chaudhari is a Fellow of the Maharashtra Academy of Sciences, IETE and IE (I), the Founder Chair of IEEE Pune Section (R-10), and a Senior Member of IEEE. He also chaired the IEEE Communications Society Pune Chapter. He serves as a Program Evaluator of the Engineering Accreditation Commission (EAC) of ABET, United States, for accreditation of computer, communications, and similar engineering programs. He has been part of ABET Teams for onsite accreditation at several U.S. and other foreign Universities. He has also undertaken NAAC accreditation peer team visits to various colleges and Universities in India. He has been on the panel of juries of several prestigious national awards and as a member of multiple committees related to higher education, research, and administration established by various universities/agencies.

His doctoral research work was on Optical Solitons in Nonlinear Optical Materials. He has qualified the intensely competitive National Eligibility Test required for a teaching position in India. He has supervised many students for Masters dissertation and one student has been awarded their Ph.D under his supervision. He is currently supervising one more student for their Ph.D and one research fellow under the funded research project. Bio: Dr. Sharbani Kaushik is a renowned biotechnology researcher with expertise in bioenergy, bioelectronics, and membrane proteins. She completed her Ph.D. in the School of Energy Science and Engineering from IIT Guwahati. Her work in renewable energy and bioanalytical applications includes pioneering research on microbial fuel cells and biofuel cell biosensing devices. As a postdoctoral researcher at The Ohio State University, USA, she made significant contributions to chemistry and biochemistry, especially in membrane proteins, synthetic biology and drug discovery, resulting in multiple high-impact publications. She has also served as an Assistant Professor at the Regional Institute of Science and Technology in Meghalaya, where she introduced new courses and mentored students in biosensors and biomedical instrumentation. Dr. Kaushik has received numerous accolades, including the Young Scientist Award from the Materials Research Society of India and the ISEES Best PhD Thesis Award from the International Society of Energy Environment and Sustainability.. Her excellent presentations and publications at international conferences reflect her ability to communicate complex scientific concepts effectively. In addition to her research, Dr. Kaushik has held administrative roles, such as Travel Award Co-Chair for the Postdoctoral Association at the Ohio State University and Departmental PhD Representative to the Student Academic Board, IIT Guwahati. Her extensive publications in prestigious journals and book chapters highlight her contributions to sustainable energy and membrane protein biogenesis. Dr. Kaushik remains dedicated to advancing science through her research and education, driving innovations in bioelectrochemical devices and sustainable energy solutions.

Bio: Dr. Akshay Ramesh Bura is an Assistant Professor in Civil Engineering with over 11 years of combined teaching and research experience at premier technical institutions in India. He earned his Ph.D. in Civil Engineering from Sardar Vallabhbhai National Institute of Technology (SVNIT), Surat, where his doctoral research focused on carbonation-induced corrosion behaviour of reinforced concrete, with particular emphasis on CO₂ sequestration, durability assessment, and electrochemical characterization techniques. He holds a B.Tech. degree in Civil Engineering from Walchand College of Engineering, Sangli, Maharashtra. His research experience includes postdoctoral work at the Indian Institute of Technology (IIT) Madras, contributing to advanced studies on low-carbon and durable cementitious materials. Dr. Bura has served as Assistant Professor at Visvesvaraya National Institute of Technology (VNIT), Nagpur, and Vishwakarma Institute of Information Technology (VIIT), Pune. In recognition of his research excellence in corrosion science and durability of concrete structures, he was awarded the prestigious NACE Foundation India Scholarship (2021) by the NACE International Foundation, Houston, USA, conferred on promising young researchers for impactful contributions in corrosion engineering and materials durability. He is the renowned Director of Photography for ‘Kerala Story’ and has been a part of the Indian film industry for over 35 years. Mohapatra grew up toying with photography in a family-owned photo studio. Later he indulged in art and literature that drew him towards cinema that culminated in a degree from FTII (1992) with specialization in Cinematography. In between professional cinematography, he pursued teaching cinema as guest faculty across India, including at FTII. Awards : 1.‘BREATHING WITHOUT AIR’, a short film as co-director won 2 Best Short Film Awards at New York and Paris in 2003. 2. Worked as a Cinematographer for several award winning films of National level : ‘NILAMADHABA’, the Biopic of Sunanda Patnaik, by Late Dilip Patnaik won National Award for Best Documentary in 2011. ‘HELLO ARSI’, the last noted Odia film by Sambit Mahanty bagged 3 National Awards in 2018. ‘ANUKAMPAN’ by Balaka Ghosh, won National Awards as Best Cultural Film in 1993. Diploma Film ‘AAMUKH’ won 1991 National Film Awards for Short Film on Social Issue.

Name: Dr. Samarth Dilip Patwardhan
Bio: Samarth D. Patwardhan serves as Head of Centre for Subsea Engineering Research (CSER), and Professor in the Department of Petroleum Engineering at MITWPU, Pune, India. His research interests include production and reservoir engineering, enhanced oil recovery, HSE, as well as applying data analytics to the oil and gas domain. Through research grants he has procured; he has been instrumental in revamping the reservoir characterization laboratory and upgrading the simulation lab with industry-benchmarked software tools at the department. He is involved in collaborating with industry to further the academic and research partnerships for the recently commissioned CSER lab, a one-of-its-kind lab established through a common shared vision with Aker Solutions. Further, his current efforts are also directed towards setting up a stateof-the-art research lab for testing various characteristics of Nano-dusts, which span across industries. The lab is jointly funded by the Department of Science and Technology (DST), Government of India (GoI), and Techniche Engineering Private Limited (TEPL), an HSE company based out of Pune, India. He works closely with his undergraduate, graduate and doctorate students on topics spanning from characterizing various rock types using data analytics, to enhanced oil recovery, and applying computational fluid dynamics to problems being faced in the oil and gas industry. He serves as a reviewer on multiple prestigious peer-reviewed journals and funding agencies and is involved in collaborative work on research proposals on multiple platforms, including academia and industry, both at national and international levels. He is the recipient of the 2019 APJ Abdul Kalam MIT WPU Research and Innovation Award, and the SPE 2022 Regional Distinguished Achievement Award for Petroleum Engineering Faculty for South Asia and Pacific Region. Samarth serves as a Member on the Enhanced Recovery Committee (ERC), formed under the Ministry of Petroleum and Natural Gas (MoPNG), Government of India (GoI), Director on the SPE International Mumbai Section board, Faculty Advisor to the MITWPU – SPE Student Chapter, and a Member on the Energy4Me committee formed for South Asia, under SPE International. Apart from serving as a SPE Student Chapter Faculty Advisor since 2014, he has volunteered for multiple activities within SPE, including acting in the capacity of a judge for Regional Student Paper Contest (RSPC) for all categories (U.G., P.G., and Ph.D.) since 2017, as well as volunteering under SPE Cares initiative. Through industry support, he has been instrumental in organizing the RSPC at the MITWPU campus in 2014, as well as planning and organizing multiple technical workshops, guest lectures and field visits for student members, keeping up with SPE’s mission of disseminating and exchanging knowledge concerning oil and gas industry, to build technical and professional competence in the next generation workforce, thereby bridging the gap between industry and academics. Over several years, he has inspired student members to undertake activities like tree plantations, donation drives, and cleanliness drives under the banner of SPE Cares, instilling in them a feeling of caring for the planet, and giving back to both nature and society. Under his guidance, MITWPU SPE Student Chapter carried out the first ever “Pink Energy4Me” drive for female high school students in Pune and Mumbai, and the largest ever Energy4Me drive, which was appreciated in the form of a special mention in the SPE publication “The Way Ahead”. This led to a positive impact of having generated curiosity and interest within the high school students, especially females, in considering Petroleum Engineering and upstream oil and gas industry as a possible career choice. His leadership and involvement have led to the MITWPU Student Chapter winning both the SPE Gold as well as Outstanding Awards multiple times. Prior to joining academics in India, he has worked with Schlumberger Technology Corporation, both in the U.S., as well as in India, in various roles including consulting and well services. Samarth holds a Bachelors in Mechanical Engineering from University of Pune, a Masters in Engineering Management from University of Missouri-Rolla, a Masters in Petroleum Engineering from University of Tulsa, and a Doctorate in Petroleum Engineering from Indian Institute of Technology Madras. Education Qualifications : Ph.D. from Indian Institute of Technology (IIT) Madras.

Bio: "Dr. Shikha Vikrant Gaikwad is a distinguished microbiologist and senior educationist with over 18 years of academic and research experience. She currently serves as an Assistant Professor in the Department of Biosciences and Technology, Dr. Vishwanath Karad MIT World Peace University, Pune, where she also coordinates postgraduate program of Microbiology. She has doctorate degree in Microbiology. Her expertise spans in the fields of Agriculture, Health care, Plant growth Promontory Bacteria (PGPB), Biocontrol agents, Biostimulants, Bioprocess Technology, Circular Economy, and Metabolomics, Plant–Microbe Interactions. Dr. Gaikwad has made notable contributions to microbial biosurfactants, focusing on their isolation, optimization, and sustainable applications in agriculture and bioremediation. Her research further explores bioactive microbial metabolites such as β-glucans and melanin, emphasizing their potential in drug delivery, immunotherapy, and cosmetic biotechnology. She has pioneered eco-friendly bioprocesses, including hydrodynamic cavitation-based polymer extraction and biosurfactant-assisted remediation of polluted environments. She has successfully led several funded research projects under BCUD-SPPU, ONGC Chair MIT, and MIT-WPU Innovation and Seed Grant programs, resulting in international publications, patents, and culture depositions with CSIR–NCL and NCBI. Dr. Gaikwad’s goals focus on advancing research-integrated learning, fostering curriculum innovation aligned with global education standards, and promoting sustainable biomanufacturing and environmental stewardship in line with UN SDGs (SDG 3 – Good Health and Well-being, SDG 6 – Clean Water and Sanitation, SDG 9 – Industry, Innovation, and Infrastructure, SDG 13 – Climate Action, and SDG 15 – Life on Land), promoting sustainable biomanufacturing and environmental stewardship. She aims to mentor young researchers and strengthen interdisciplinary education for societal benefit. Bio: Dr. Amruta Naik is working as an Assistant Professor at the Department of Biosciences and Technology, MIT-WPU, Pune. She is a goal-driven researcher and academician with a research experience of around 12 years in the field of Stem Cell Biology and Bone Biology. Dr. Amruta has received Ph.D. in Biotechnology from the University of Pune. Her research interests mainly include invention of new strategies for the application of Mesenchymal Stem Cells for the treatment of bone degenerative disorders to get better therapeutic effects. Dr. Amruta has received two research grants from DBT and DST, Govt. of India for perusing research in the field of stem cell biology and regenerative medicine. During her post-doctoral research work, she was also involved in collaborative research projects that studied the in vitro biocompatibility and osteointegration of scaffolds for bone and cartilage regeneration. She has published 14 research and review articles in peer-reviewed journals of international repute. Currently Dr. Amruta Naik is serving as a Guest Editor for Cancer Reports (Wiley) and JoVE. Bio: Dr. Kunal Modak holds a Ph.D. in Structural Geology from IIT ISM Dhanbad, where he conducted research on the structural geometry, structural mapping, deformation, paleopeizometry, and metamorphism of the Mesoproterozoic Kaladgi Basin. His work provided critical insights into basin evolution and its implications for hydrocarbon and mineral exploration. He also holds an MSc in Geology and an M.Tech in Petroleum Exploration from IIT ISM Dhanbad, equipping him with a strong foundation in both fundamental geological processes and their applications in petroleum systems. He has over 6 years of experience as a scientist under the Ministry of Earth Sciences, where he worked on the prestigious "Scientific Deep Drilling in Koyna Intraplate Seismic Zone" project. His research in this project focused on understanding the mechanisms of reservoir-triggered seismicity through core logging, petrography, microstructural analysis, SEM, and EDS. His research contributions include both single-author and leading-author publications, including a 2022 paper proposing a hypothetical 5 km deep borehole in the Koyna region to study reservoir-triggered seismicity. He also serves as a reviewer for several reputed peer-reviewed journals, contributing to the advancement of geoscientific research. Bio: Dr. Parul Jadhav is an associate professor with almost 30 years of experience at Dr. Vishwanath Karad MIT World Peace University. She has held various roles in academics, restructuring, research, operations, and accreditation, and has successfully led several portfolios at the Faculty of Engineering and Technology (FoET). Dr. Jadhav's research interests include Artificial Intelligence, Machine Learning, Deep Learning Architecture, Video and Image Analytics, Compression Techniques, and Signal Processing. She has published over 30 papers in international journals/conferences, holds three patents, and has multiple datasets/copyrights. Her research has been recognized through grants from organizations such as the Department of Science & Technology, BCUD, ASPIRE, and KIRAN Division - Women Scientists Scheme. She designed the Post Graduate Diploma in AI&ML, which was created in collaboration with Infosys, and has established many Labs across universities, where she is regarded as an expert in embedded signal processing. She has also conducted many faculty development programs and is a reviewer for Elsevier and IEEE journals. Dr. Jadhav contributed significantly to academic restructuring at the FoET, aligning the academic structure of engineering programs with the National Education Policy framework. She was instrumental in implementing Outcome Based Education (OBE) processes, training and change management, and computing learning outcomes through courses and assessments. Dr. Jadhav has also been at the forefront of national and international accreditation for the department. She completed her Bachelor’s, Master’s, and Doctoral degrees with an exemplary academic record from College of Engineering Pune (CoEP) and has received numerous awards and recognition for her work. She is an outgoing person with excellent leadership capabilities and has good connections with peers, students, and seniors. Bio: Sudhirkumar Shinde earned his master's degree in Organic Chemistry from Shivaji University in Kolhapur, Maharashtra, India. Following this, he worked as a project assistant in the Controlled Release Technology group of the Polymer Science and Engineering division at the National Chemical Laboratory in Pune, India from 2003-2006. Shinde then received his Ph.D. in 2013 from the Technical University of Dortmund in Germany, where he worked with Professor Börje Sellergren in the Department of Chemistry and Chemical Biology. As a Ph.D. exchange fellow, he also worked in the Department of Medicinal Chemistry and Chemical Biology at Utrecht University in the Netherlands, broadening his research interests to include polymers, molecular recognition, bioanalysis, and bio-interfaces for biomedical applications. Shinde then worked as a postdoctoral research fellow at the Biofilms Research Centre for Biointerfaces at Malmö University in Sweden from June 2013 to June 2018. During this time, he also spent time as a visiting scholar at Ruhr-Universität Bochum in Germany, working with Professor Katrin Marcus in the Medizinische Proteom-Center Funktionelle Proteomik. Shinde was involved in several European Training Network projects, including NEMOPUR, PEPMIP, BIOCAPTURE, and GlycoImaging, which were funded by the European Commission through the Marie Skłodowska-Curie Action. From June 2018 to September 2020, Shinde was a Swan Teaching Fellow and Postdoctoral Research Fellow at the School of Chemistry and Chemical Engineering at Queen's University in Belfast, Northern Ireland, UK. Currently, he is an Associate Professor at the School of Consciousness at MIT World Peace University in Pune, India. His research interests include molecular imprinting, supramolecular chemistry, biomaterials, polymer chemistry, smart polymers for biomedical applications and bioprocesses, as well as functional and intelligent nanomaterials. Shinde has independently led more than 12 research projects and holds two patents. He has also published over 30 peer-reviewed scientific papers in top journals such as Angew. Chem., J. Am. Chem. Soc., Anal. Chem., ACS Appl. Mater. Interfaces, ACS Appl. Polym. Mater., Analyst, J. Chrom. A and B, Chem. Eu. J., Chem Eng J., among others. Furthermore, Shinde has been involved in technology transfers and innovations, pitching two business ideas in the area of life sciences. He has won verification grants twice from Lund University Innovation Systems in Lund, Sweden, and contributed to developing commercial technology in the healthcare sector with a private US company. Shinde also serves as a reviewer for leading chemistry and materials chemistry journals.

Bio: Dr. Amit Kumar is working as an Assistant Professor at the Department of Biosciences and Technology, MIT-WPU, Pune. After clearing the CSIR NET-JRF exam, he obtained his Ph.D. degree in Plant Molecular Biology from IISER Pune with Best PhD thesis gold medal award in 2020. During his PhD tenure he worked to understand how plants respond to photoperiod and change their developmental program mediated by epigenetic modifications and microRNAs with special focus on potato development pathway. Next to this, he went to Wageningen University in Netherlands to pursue his postdoctoral research focused on understanding the role of histone acetylation and methylation during heat induced haploid embryogenesis. During his postdoc tenure he also collaborated with researchers at Max Planck Institute of Plant Physiology at Potsdam Germany to study the effect of heat shock factors (HSFs) in regulating the thermomemory response in plants. Dr. Amit returned to India in 2023 upon receiving the prestigious INSPIRE faculty fellowship award sponsored by DST and started working in the department of Plant Molecular Biology at the University of Delhi South Campus. He has over ten years of research expertise in various molecular biology techniques, gene editing techniques and bioinformatics analysis of multi-omics datasets. His present area of research is aimed at understanding the genetic and epigenetic factors regulating the haploid embryogenesis and plant cell totipotency, with ultimate aim to speed up the plant breeding programs and achieve sustainable global food security.

Bio: Dr. Apurv Chaitanya Nellikka received his Integrated M.Sc. in Physics from Amrita University in 2012. His research includes generating and characterizing single photon sources, studying entangled photons, and designing nanoplasmonic devices that exhibit quantum behaviors. Additionally, he explores the generation of exotic light beams with challenging temporal and spatial profiles.

Bio: Dr. Abhishek Singh, works as an Assistant Professor of Statistics at the Department of Mathematics and Statistics, MIT World Peace University (MIT-WPU). With a passion for data analysis and a deep understanding of statistical methodologies, Dr. Abhishek significantly contributes to the field of statistics and its applications. Having completed a Ph.D. in Statistics from a prestigious Indian Institute of Technology (Indian School of Mines) Dhanbad, Dr. Abhishek brings a wealth of knowledge and expertise to the MIT-WPU community. Also, Dr. Abhishek has done his B.Sc. ((Stats, Mathes, and Computer Science), (Hons. Statistics)) and M.Sc. (Statistics) from Banaras Hindu University. He has qualified in Gate mathematics too and his knowledge of mathematics and statistics is fostering students as well as the department. He has expertise in C/C++, Fortran, R, Python, & Sagemath, Statistical Machine Learning, SPSS, SQL. His research interests lie at the intersection of theoretical and applied statistics, focusing on developing innovative statistical models and methodologies to address complex real-world problems. He has a total 10 publications in reputed journals (SCI/SCIE) and 8 papers (2 papers are completed by M.Sc. students) are under review, especially focused on estimating the finite population parameters using auxiliary characteristics in various sampling techniques. He has given a new sampling method that is neutrosophic ranked set sampling for uncertain/indeterminant/fuzzy/vague data. Dr. Abhishek's research areas/interests are sampling, ranked set sampling, inference, statistical quality control, time series/forecasting, statistics, fuzzy statistics, neutrosophic statistics, data science and machine learning. Also, he believes in the power of collaboration and often engage in interdisciplinary collaborations to tackle complex problems that require expertise from multiple domains. Dr. Abhishek is a reviewer in many national and international journals like soft computing, PlosOne, Heliyon, Mathematical population studies, Thailand statistician, Neutrosophic sets & systems, and in Mathematical Problem in Engineering. Dr. Abhishek views teaching and research as interconnected pillars of academic excellence. His research informs his teaching with the latest advancements, while teaching sparks new ideas and fosters collaboration. By involving students in research, he aims to nurture statisticians skilled in theory and practical problem-solving. Through these efforts, he strives to contribute to MIT-WPU’s mission of academic and societal growth, empowering students as skilled professionals and responsible global citizens.

Bio: Dr. Kausik Bhattacharyya is an Assistant Professor at the Department of Biosciences and Technology (DoBT) and Revvity – MIT-WPU Centre of Excellence for Bioimaging Technologies and Innovation. Serving additionally as a Departmental Placement coordinator for the department of Biosciences and Technology, Dr Kausik has more than 12 years of research experience in Infectious Disease biology, Microbiology, Genomics and Bioinformatics and 7 years of teaching experience. He has completed his Ph.D. from Department of Biomedical Sciences (ACBR), University of Delhi. During his Ph.D., he has demonstrated how genomic sequence and novel genomic variations can have functional significance in Multi-Drug Resistant (MDR) clinical isolates of M. tuberculosis through Bioinformatics and Experimental approaches, including altering protein 3D structure, causing drug resistance, altering host-pathogen interactions, Molecular mimicry, and Evasion of Immune responses. Before joining Ph.D., he worked as a junior Team Mentor and Project Fellow in the area of drug discovery against Tuberculosis (OSDD), a CSIR-led Team India Consortium with global participation. (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Open_Source_Drug_Discovery) at Institute of Genomics and Integrative Biology (IGIB), Delhi and Institute of Microbial Technology (IMTECH), Chandigarh. He has contributed to the development of India's first consolidated Genetic Disease Database (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indian_Genetic_Disease_Database) during his research at Indian Institute of Chemical biology (IICB), Kolkata. Dr. Kausik has 3 years of Post-Doctoral research experience at Indian Institute of Technology (IIT) Delhi, Indian Institute of Science (IISc), Bangalore and SSSIHL, Puttaparthi where he worked on habitat-specific bacterial behaviour, bacterial gene expression and Anti-Microbial Resistance (AMR). Dr Kausik trained students in different Bioinformatics and Molecular biology workshops. Dr Kausik has worked with different Industry experts during his research journey. Currently, Dr Kausik works in the amalgamation of both Bioinformatics as well as Experimental approaches in the area of Bacterial and Viral genomics. Subjects Taught 1. Genomics and proteomics 2. Bio: Dr. Kunal Gaurav is a Professor of Marketing & Strategy at the School of Business, MIT World Peace University, Pune. He holds a PhD in Business Administration and an MBA earned with top academic honours. His teaching and research interests span Strategic Management, Digital Transformation, Digital Marketing, and Customer Relationship Management (CRM). He is widely recognized for integrating emerging industry trends with pedagogical innovation, particularly in the areas of blended learning and faculty development. Dr. Gaurav is also actively engaged in editorial and advisory roles and has contributed to institutional development through research mentoring, curriculum design, and leadership of national and international conferences. His work exemplifies a deep commitment to academic excellence, innovation, and impactful education.

Furthermore, he has applied for two international patents, including 'Reliability Indicator Device For Disk Brake In Modern Vehicles' and 'Development of Multifunctional Gas cylinder stand with Leak detection and scaling mechanism.' Chetan is a true innovator who is passionate about improving engineering designs to make them safer, more efficient, and more reliable.

Bio: Dr. Pankaj Koparde is an Evolutionary Ecologist working with core expertise in subjects such as Urban Ecology, Biogeography, Conservation Science, Biodiversity Informatics, and Science Communication. He primarily works on owls and dragonflies. He is an admin of two mega citizen science projects, DragonflySouthAsia and OwlIndia. He is a TEDx speaker and has delivered talks across popular platforms such as Towards and Ecological Landscape (TEL), Indian Society of Landscape Architects (ISOLA), and Science on Tap. He is a DST Young Scientist awardee; SAEVUS Rising Star of Conservation; Prakriti & EarthWatch Fellow. He is an IUCN contributor and actively engaged in research benefitting on-ground conservation. His work is featured in several newspapers and magazines. In their latest study his team discovered a new species of damselfly and named it after Ecological Armageddon. He is a member of two government committees such as the Panchagani Biodiversity Committee and Pashan Lake Conservation Committee. He is a member of the World Dragonfly Association USA, International Biogeography Society USA, and Society for Conservation Biology UK. He also works as an ecological consultant & subject matter expert with various organizations such as ERM, Ramboll, Ranwa, and corporates. He is also a published Marathi writer with a major interest in literary essays (Lalit). His lab group is known as Chatur Ullu Lab denoting the off beat research Dr. Koparde and his team is doing on Dragonflies (Chatur) and Owls (Ullu). Education : MSc Biotechnology (2010), IBB, SPPU Pune PhD in Ecology & Evolution (2019), Manipal Academy of Higher Education (MAHE) in collaboration with Salim Ali Center for Ornithology & Natural History (SACON) and National Center for Biological Sciences (NCBS), TIFR Bangalore PGD in Data Science (2022), RISE WPU & KPMG Netherlands

Name: Dr. Meera JeevanReddy Chintala
Bio: Dr. Miss Meera currently works as an assistant professor of civil engineering at Dr. Vishwanath Karad MIT World Peace University, Pune, India, and heads Building Materials & Sustainability (BM&S) team. The researchers of BM&S Group are devoted to elucidating the fundamental science and performance of sustainable building materials. The research mainly focuses on developing green concrete utilizing various wastes through experimentation and implementing AI&ML. Before Joining as an assistant professor, she worked as a research scientist at Shriram Institute for Industrial Research, New Delhi, and developed a strength prediction model for hardened mortar by determining reactive silica content. Dr. Miss Meera holds a Ph.D. in Civil Engineering from the Indian Institute of Technology Delhi (IIT Delhi), New Delhi, India. Her Ph.D. research, titled “Non-structural concrete utilizing fly ash, marble powder, and foam” encompasses a unified theory of designing normal and low-density non-structural concrete with supplementary cementitious materials and mineral admixtures. It includes an “industrial sustainability method” of producing optimized concrete mixes and also presents a new method of assessing the durability of concrete. Dr. Miss Meera has a Master of Technology in Civil Engineering with Structural Engineering specialization from the National Institute of Technology Rourkela, Odisha, India, and a Bachelor of Technology in Civil Engineering from Biju Patnaik University of Technology, Rourkela, Odisha. She is a member of ASCE, ICE, ACI, ISTRUCTE, ICI, SEFI, and RILEM. She has also contributed to different groups working on Composites and Reinforce concrete. Qualification : Ph.D. Specific research interest on: 1. Macro & Micro mechanics of concrete 2. The durability of concrete structures 3. Green building materials 4. Material optimization 5. Waste utilization and sustainability studies 6. Concrete composites Services offered at Building Materials & Sustainability (BM&S): 1. Consultancy and Sponsored R&Ds – Concrete mix design, material management, Designing and Proof checking of structures, NDT and Durability analysis of structures, Planning and cost evaluation of projects, Sustainability analysis & Waste utilization 2. Training, workshops/ skill development programs for industry-sponsored candidates 3. Internships for students.Students interested in internships, Research, and Ph.D. can contact me! Name: Dr. Kirtikumar Kondhare
Bio: Dr. Kirtikumar Ramesh Kondhare is working as an Assistant Professor at the Department of Biosciences and Technology, MIT-WPU from 22nd Sept. 2025. He completed Ph.D. in 2012 from Harper Adams University in collaboration with Rothamsted Research, United Kingdom. After returning to India in 2013, he worked as a Post-doc Fellow at IISER Pune for 6 years. From 2019 onwards, he worked as a DST Inspire Faculty and Assistant Professor, AcSIR at CSIR-National Chemical Laboratory Pune. During his DST Inspire Faculty tenure, he also worked as a Visiting Scientist at the Plant & Environmental Sciences Department of Weizmann Institute of Science, Israel for five months (May-Oct 2023). Dr. Kondhare has published 26 research articles / review papers in Peer-reviewed international journals and wrote 3 book chapters. From 2019 until 2025, he served as an independent PI for DST Inspire Faculty grant (35 Lakhs) on investigating the role of two phytohormones auxin and strigolactone on storage root development and sprouting in sweetpotato. He also contributed a Co-PI for five CSIR research grants (~550 lakhs) focused on Crop improvement and crop protection in various plants, such as tomato, potato, and a medicinal plant - Glory lily. In 2022, Dr. Kondhare was elected with two prestigious Young Scientist awards: (i) NASI Young Scientist Platinum Jubilee Award from National Academy of Sciences, Allahabad and (ii) Young Associate from Maharashtra Academy of Sciences, Pune, for his significant research contribution on tuber formation mechanisms and yield enhancement in potato and storage root development in sweetpotato. Dr. Kondhare is also serving as Young Scientist Editorial Board Member for Plant Hormones journal, Maximum Academic Press Journal (Term: 2 years from April 1, 2025, to March 31, 2027). He also serves as a peer reviewer for several reputed International journals, such as Nature Plants, Current Opinion in Plant Biology, New Phytologist, The Plant Journal, Physiology of Plantarum, Plant Physiology and Biochemistry, Physiology and Molecular Biology of Plants, International Journal of Biological Macromolecules, Scientific Reports, BMC Plant Biology, Genomics, International Journal of Molecular Sciences, Molecules, Plant Science, Journal of Cereal Science, Agriculture, Plant Biology, Horticulturae, Plant Signaling and Behavior. Research Interests : Understanding the molecular mechanism of storage root development and sprouting in sweetpotato (Ipomoea batatas) and allied storage root crops utilizing transcriptomics, metabolomics, molecular tools, genome-editing approaches, and plant transformation techniques. Overall focus is to enhance the yield, shelf-life, nutritional quality and bioactive compounds in important tuber, rhizome, and storage root crops/plants for societal benefits. Research Papers : 1. Name: Mrs. Sulakshana Sagar Malwade
Bio: Prof. Sagar Kolapkar is an Assistant Professor in the School of Civil Engineering, MIT World Peace University, Pune. He received his B.E. in Civil Engineering (2010) from Pune University and M.Tech (Transportation Systems Engineering) in 2013 from IIT Guwahati. His research focuses on Parking Demand Management and Supply Regulation and Warm Mix Asphalt. He is a certified Road Safety Auditor by Ministry of Road Transport and Highways and Indian Roads Congress. He has actively worked with Pune Municipal Corporation on Parking Policy. He qualified GATE in 2011 and has published several research papers in top-ranked journals in Civil Engineering. He has been an active reviewer of international journal Materials Today (Elsevier). He has written a book on Advanced Transportation Engineering. He actively working as Infrastructure Cordinator at School of Civil Engineering. Patent "ATC – SYSTEM: Advanced Traffic Control System By Using Intelligent, Technology, CPWS- Elements: Conversion of Plastic Waste into Useful Structural Elements for Construction Industry”

Name: Mr. Akash Dixit
Bio: Mr. Akash Dixit is an Assistant Professor at the School of Law, MIT-World Peace University. He completed his LLM in Business Laws from National Law University, Delhi, and holds a B.A. LL.B with a specialization in Energy Laws from the University of Petroleum and Energy Studies, Dehradun. He qualified for the UGC NET exam in 2022. Name: Dr. Ajendra Singh
Bio: Dr. Ajendra Singh is an emerging scholar and researcher in the domain of petroleum engineering, with a specialized focus on reservoir characterization, CO₂ sequestration, and subsurface flow modeling. Currently serving as an Assistant Professor at MIT World Peace University, Pune, Dr. Singh contributes to the academic development of future engineers through instruction in core petroleum subjects, software integration, and laboratory training. His academic engagements are deeply interwoven with research-led teaching and experiential learning. Dr. Singh earned his Ph.D. in Petroleum Engineering from Pandit Deendayal Energy University (PDEU), Gandhinagar, where his research included investigation of bioturbation-induced heterogeneities in clastic reservoirs using advanced techniques such as Micro-CT imaging, NMR, and high-pressure mercury injection (HPMI). His doctoral work contributed significantly to understanding pore-scale processes affecting reservoir quality and enhanced oil recovery potential in the Cretaceous Bhuj Formation of the Kachchh Basin. He holds an M. Tech in Petroleum Engineering from RGIPT, Raebareli, and a B.Sc. in Mechanical Engineering from Dayalbagh Educational Institute, Agra. Before joining MIT World Peace University, Dr. Singh was engaged in multiple research-intensive roles. At IIT Bombay, as a Project Scientist (2023–2025), where he led multidisciplinary research on CO₂ injection in deep saline aquifers, focusing on geomechanical and geochemical feedback mechanisms through core-flooding experiments and numerical simulation using CMG (GEM and STAR). His work contributed to predictive modeling of CO₂ plume behavior and its implications for carbon capture and storage (CCS) in onshore Indian sedimentary basins.In his tenure as a Domain Expert at PDEU, Dr. Singh was involved in basin-scale petroleum system modeling of the Kutch and Saurashtra basins using Schlumberger Petrel and Petromod. His responsibilities included seismic interpretation, reservoir property modeling, and uncertainty quantification in resource estimation under PRMS guidelines. His analytical rigor extended to consultancy roles, including experimental investigation of formation damage mechanisms at EMC India Pvt. Ltd. Dr. Singh has authored and co-authored numerous peer-reviewed publications in high-impact journals, including Journal of Petroleum Science and Engineering, Geoenergy Science and Engineering, Geoheritage, and Journal of Earth System Science. His interdisciplinary research has been presented at international forums such as the European Association of Geoscientists & Engineers (EAGE), Society of Petroleum Geophysicists (SPG), and GEOINDIA. He holds an Indian patent for “GeoCPR”, a methodological innovation for extracting geothermal attributes from petrophysical datasets. His early research career includes technical roles at ONGC’s Institute of Reservoir Studies, Ahmedabad and RGIPT, Raebareli where he engaged in seismic data processing, well log interpretation, and dynamic simulation of Cambay Basin reservoirs. His proficiency spans advanced geoscientific software platforms, including Schlumberger Petrel, CMG, Eclipse, Petromod, and IHS Kingdom. Dr. Singh is an active member of professional bodies including the Society of Petroleum Engineers (SPE) and Petrotech Society of India. He has received accolades for academic excellence and professional contributions, including international recognition as a finalist team leader in the 2023 EAGE Laurie Dake Challenge and participation in the SHARP CCS workshop hosted by GEUS, Denmark. Through a combination of research, teaching, and technical practice, Dr. Singh continues to contribute to the advancement of reservoir engineering, with an emphasis on low-carbon energy transition and integrated subsurface resource management. Education Qualifications : Ph.D. from Pandit Deendayal Energy University (PDEU), Gandhinagar.

Bio: Dr. Bishnudeo Roy, an Assistant Professor at the Department of Biosceinces and Technology, MIT-WPU, Pune, holds research experience of more than sixteen years in the area of B cell immunology and immunemodulation by various biomolecules. After having obtained a Ph.D. degree in Immunology from Hannover Medical School, Hannover, Germany, in 2007, he carried his first and second postdoctoral reasearch at Helmholtz Centre for Infection Research, Braunschweig, Germany, and Oslo Oniversity Hospital, Oslo, Norway, respectively. His doctoral and postdoctoral work focused on characterization of antibody profile of various B cell populations from mice and and humans using single cell high throughput seqeuncing. Protocol for the high throughput isolation and sequencing of paired heavy and light chain genes of individual antigen-specific plasma cells established by him was pivotal in characterizing the auto-reactive antibody repertoire genes from a few thousand B cell clones of celiac disease (an autoimmune condition) patients. Recent research publications authored/co-authored by him encompass: 1. assessment of immunization efficiency of two COVID-19 vaccinces manufactured in India 2. impact of aldosterone on macrophage survival and activation in hyperglycemic conditions 3. quantitative assessment of SARS-CoV-2 load in wastewater of Pune and 4. identification and characterization of L-asparaginase producing human commensal bacteria that can be used for anti-cancer therapy. He has published 16 research/review articles and his current h- and i-index is 9. Name: Dr. Abhijith B
Bio: Abhijith B serves as an Assistant Professor at the Dadasaheb Phalke International Film Institute, MIT-WPU. He holds a PhD in Cultural Studies from The English and Foreign Languages University, Hyderabad. His study concentrates on contemporary Malayalam cinema, particularly addressing issues of form, space, and subjectivity. By prioritising the ideology of form as a primary theoretical framework, his work analyses the historical transformations influencing Indian cinema in a broader context. His study examines the intertwining of geography and story as a crucial indicator of cinema's social component in the contemporary era, especially in the absence of concrete social markers under the neoliberal context. His study has been published in peer-reviewed journals, and he is presently examining the correlation between contemporary genre forms and the issue of political federalism in Indian cinema.

Bio: Sanjeev Kumar Shangary, Ph.D., is a Professor in the School of Consciousness at the Dr. Vishwanath Karad MIT World Peace University (MIT-WPU), Pune, India with over 25 years of cumulative experience in academics, research, and industry. He obtained a Master’s degree in Biology (Molecular Biology and Biochemistry) and a Ph.D. degree in Life Sciences, both from the Guru Nanak Dev University (GNDU), Amritsar, India. He received post-doctoral fellowship from the Centre for Cellular & Molecular Biology (CCMB), Hyderabad, India. Later, he investigated the impact of the synthetic peptides, derived from the Bcl-2 family proteins, on the chemo-resistant leukemia. He, next, joined the University of Michigan Comprehensive Cancer Center, as a research faculty (Research Investigator and later promoted to Research Assistant Professor position), where he played an instrumental role in the discovery and pre-clinical development of a novel class of small-molecule inhibitors targeting the MDM2-p53 interaction for the treatment of cancer. Subsequently, he joined the R&D Oncology division of the Piramal Enterprises Ltd, Mumbai, India as an Assistant Director, and led a team on several cancer drug discovery programs. Prior to joining the MIT-WPU, he was an Associate director and team lead of the Drug Repurposing vertical at the Excelra Knowledge Solutions, Hyderabad, India. He was the recipient of the prestigious Young Investigator Award of the Melanoma Research Alliance (MRA, USA) and a research grant, as Principal Investigator, from the MRA. He also played a role as a co-investigator on the grants funded by the National Institute of Health, USA, and the Leukemia and Lymphoma Society Foundation, USA. He has served as a reviewer for several journals. He is a co-author on over 30 original research articles/reviews/book chapters and co-inventor on several patents.

Bio: Dr. Samuel Jacob Kuruvilla is an Associate Professor at the WPU School of Liberal Arts. He completed his BA, majoring in Indian History (with minors in Economics & Political Science) from CMS College, Kottayam, followed by an MA in Politics & International Relations from the School of International Relations & Politics, Mahatma Gandhi University, Kottayam. He pursued his M.Phil in Diplomacy at Jawaharlal Nehru University (JNU), New Delhi, and obtained his Ph.D. in Religion & Politics from the University of Exeter, United Kingdom. Previously, he served as a Post-Doctoral Fellow at the School of International Relations and Politics of Mahatma Gandhi University, Kottayam, Kerala. Additionally, he received his Doctorate in Politics and Theology from the University of Exeter in the United Kingdom. Dr. Kuruvilla's research interests primarily focus on West Asian Politics, the Israel-Palestine Conflict, and Indian Foreign Policy. His teaching experience encompasses Political Thought, Theory & International Relations, as well as various Area studies courses at both the Undergraduate & Postgraduate levels. He held the position of Visiting Fellow at the Manohar Parikkar Centre for Defense Studies and Analyses in New Delhi during the period January-April 2012. His life ambition is to write a history of the world from the perspective of the Global South. Dr. Kuruvilla has over 10 years of experience as an Assistant Professor of Political Science at the University of Kerala and over 10 years of separate experience as an M.Phil/Ph.D/Post-Doctoral Researcher in various reputed universities in India & the United Kingdom.

Bio: Dr. Summon Koul holds a Master's degree in Organic Chemistry from the University of Kashmir (1998) and a PhD from the University of Jammu (2003). During her doctoral research, she focused on isolating, characterizing, and semisynthetic conversions of biologically active natural products. After completing her PhD, she worked as a Research Associate at the Indian Institute of Science in Bengaluru, followed by a Postdoctoral Fellowship at Simon Fraser University in British Columbia, Canada, where she worked on the total synthesis of Triquinacenes. She has handled multi-crore projects and has been recognized for Best Awards in the Company. Her focus areas were Cardiovascular Diseases, Metabolic Disorders, and Inflammation. Currently, Summon has been working as a professor in the School of Consciousness for the past 2.5 years. She has over 16 publications in international journals of repute, book chapters, and eight patents to her credit.

Bio: Dr. Parineeta Das has completed her doctoral study at National Institute of Technology Nagaland (NIT Nagaland). Her doctoral study focused on dendrimers, the emerging polymeric architectures having several interesting features suitable for application in many diverse fields including biomedical field. She has synthesized this polymeric architecture following the green synthetic protocols. It included designing dendritic architectures, green organic synthesis, antimicrobial, biological studies, isotherm study and computational toxicology. During her doctoral study, she has also worked as a Junior Research Fellow on the project entitled “Study of Non-edible Plant-Oils of North-East: Extraction, Compositional Characterization and Analysis for Industrial Applications” funded by North Eastern Council (NEC) in the Dept. of Science and Humanities (Chemistry), National Institute of Technology Nagaland. She has chosen this project because of the alarming concern of alkyd resins from non-renewable resources which have drawbacks such as environmental pollution, depletion of petroleum resources and even a rise in the price of petroleum-based products. In contrary, various plant seed oils are used in the production of polymers due to its renewability, biodegradability, easy availability and its cost-effective properties. The synthesized alkyd resins from the seed oils showed great potential applications in the field of paints, adhesives, coatings, and beneath water marine vessel finish that opposes salt corrosion. She has the experience of water quality survey and detection of various metal ions present in water and its elimination from it. She has given 7 oral and 2 poster presentations related to all her research work at several national and international conferences till date. She has published 5 research papers in peer-reviewed journals and 2 book chapters. She has attended various workshops, short term courses and faculty development programme. She pursued her post-graduation (M. Sc) in Chemistry, specialization in Physical Chemistry from Gauhati University and completed her graduation from Sibsagar Girls’ College, Dibrugarh University. Her research area of interest includes Polymer Science, Biopolymers, Biocatalyst, Dendrimers, Green organic synthesis, Anticorrosive coating, Biodiesel, Computational Toxicology.

Name: Dr. Atanu Hazarika
Bio: Dr. Atanu Hazarika is an Assistant Professor at the School of Business, MIT World Peace University in Pune, India. He is a Post-Doctoral Fellow from the Indian Institute of Management Bangalore. The title of the Post Doctoral research is ‘Developing sustainability-related knowledge and capability for farmers, Case Study of an Irrigation Tank project’. The project is sponsored by the Hanns Seidel Stiftung foundation (HSS), Germany. His PhD has been awarded by the Indian Institute of Technology, Kharagpur. His doctoral research work has focused on the issues of productivity and efficiency of paddy farming in Assam. His attempts to develop an interdependence (multivariate) framework for measuring the adoption rate of multiple modern technology practices. Additionally, the study attempts to find the technical efficiency and allocative efficiency level of the farmers. In addition, he worked on several projects sponsored by national and international agencies like NOVOD, SANDEE, ICSSR, and NABARD during his PhD tenure. The projects experienced give an exposure to work in different domains like the adoption and expansion behaviour of the Jatropha farmers, the economic valuation of biodiesel, the evaluation of watershed programs, and the financial risk attitude of the handloom micro-entrepreneur. He has worked as a Guest Faculty at Tezpur University, Assam. His teaching interests are Micro-economics, Macro-economics, Econometrics, Statistics, Development Economics, Operations Research, and Mathematical Economics. His research interests lie in the areas of Economics of Decision Choice, Efficiency and Productivity Analyses, Biofuel, Supply Chain, and Economic Valuation. Teaching Philosophy As an educator, Dr. Hazarika envisages a highly participatory approach to learning and teaching.
